curated-fs-kalam-gf-zen-antique: Zen Antique reads literary and dense, hairline serifs perched on heavy black stems. Kalam brings a cozy, hand-drawn looseness up top (a tech startup wordmark, maybe), while the text serif behind it does the sharp, nib-pressed work of carrying a page.
curated-fs-khand-gf-abhaya-libre: Abhaya Libre turns its thick-thin contrast up as far as it goes, fat stems against hairlines. Over a long passage, Abhaya Libre feels dignified and editorial, while Khand above it stays crisp, tightly spaced and cut at a single stroke width.
curated-fs-khand-gf-alike-angular: Authoritative and traditional, Alike Angular leans on a modest swing between its boldest and faintest strokes. Khand's flat, unmodulated lines sit above it like laser-cut sheet, so the headline feels crisp while the text serif below keeps its curves held open.
curated-fs-khand-gf-cardo: Cardo is literary and dignified, with softly varied strokes. Khand's ruler-straight lines sit above it, crisp and contemporary, and a longer read of Cardo (a product requirements document, say) stays open, connected and unhurried.
curated-fs-khand-gf-charis-sil: Bookish and dignified, Charis SIL shows a slight but noticeable stroke contrast that never turns dramatic. And Khand, cut at a single depth with tight spacing, keeps the headline crisp while the serif carries a long read without strain.
curated-fs-khand-gf-diphylleia: Diphylleia has a classic, bookish look, with a measured swell from hairline to stem and apertures that stay open even when tiny. Khand's pen never changes pressure, so the long read stays gentle.
curated-fs-khand-gf-gentium-book-plus: Khand sets a crisp, contemporary headline, its stems and arcs moving in lockstep with tight spacing. Gentium Book Plus follows with lighter horizontals and wide letter openings, which keeps a longer stretch of text traditional and easy on the eye.
curated-fs-khand-gf-gupter: Gupter feels traditional and editorial, with a visible gap at the end of every c and tightly set tracking. Khand does crisp, flat-weighted headlines best (a sticker sheet, perhaps), while Gupter's text serif does its best work in tapered, gently weighted lines.
curated-fs-khand-gf-ibarra-real-nova: Ibarra Real Nova reads editorial and traditional, with a strong pull between fat strokes and slender ones. Over a longer stretch, Ibarra Real Nova keeps its bowls unclosed and inviting, a text serif with enough contrast to hold interest below Khand's uniform lines.
curated-fs-khand-gf-mate: Mate reads editorial and dignified, its round letters cupped rather than clenched. Khand is best at crisp, constant-width headlines (a feasibility study, say), while Mate is best at soft, gradual weight changes that carry a serif paragraph.
